issue_plan.name: Take plumbing on configured repositories
issue_plan.summary: These ten issues let the factory plan, build, check and review plumbing on GitHub repositories written in Go, Python or TypeScript, including monorepos. A reviewed file on the base branch supplies each part's toolchain, locked dependencies, checks and repository rules; dependency installation alone gets network access. Native acceptance tests must fail on the base and pass after the build, while scope, ratification and human merges protect the trusted base. Init drafts the configuration and writes the CI gate, and external plumbing is enabled only after these pieces work together. Repositories without the file retain today's answer, and Invariant's existing plumbing and modeled-project builds retain their behavior.

issues.title: Define repository checks from the base branch
issues.body:
Issue #452 replaces Invariant-only plumbing with an explicit repository contract. Add a versioned .invariant/repository.json format and a shared validated loader. Each part declares its directory, Go/Python/TypeScript language, digest-pinned toolchain image, lockfile and installation inputs, install command, format/lint/build/test commands, and a command for one named test. It must also be possible to identify the repository's agent rules, current-state documents and additional trusted paths. Commands may explicitly declare an inapplicable check; an omitted required check is an error.

Load authority from a committed base snapshot, never the builder's candidate. Expose that context for later sandbox, plan, scope and agent callers. Define deterministic ownership of touched paths, including planned new files, deletions, nested parts, shared files and workspace lockfiles, so a change cannot silently select no applicable checks. Keep repository configuration distinct from modeled-project manifests. Retain an explicit Invariant compatibility path with its current commands and policies; adding this contract does not yet enable external plumbing.

Acceptance: valid single-part fixtures for all three languages and a mixed Go/TypeScript fixture load; missing and malformed files are distinguishable; unsupported languages, mutable image tags, escaping or linked paths, and ambiguous ownership fail clearly. A candidate edit cannot replace the captured base commands or trust declarations. Existing Invariant manifests and plumbing continue to load unchanged.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Install locked dependencies in an isolated cached step
issues.body:
Build dependency preparation for the repository contract from the preceding issue. The current plumbing sandbox only mounts Invariant's Go cache, which cannot supply another repository's dependencies. Use internal/toolchain/python_deps.go as a cache and isolation precedent, without inheriting its allowance for floating Python requirements or changing the Python modeled-application gate.

For each selected part, run its declared installation from locked dependency inputs in the pinned toolchain. This is the only repository-command stage with network access. It must not resolve floating dependencies, rewrite locks, or publish a reusable cache after a failed install. Cache by lockfile content, additionally separating image digest, platform, install recipe and other dependency inputs that affect the result. Pin and verify the resulting environment's identity before reuse. Candidate builds cannot poison a shared dependency cache; later checks use isolated copies or immutable dependency artifacts.

Support locked installation for Go, Python and TypeScript fixtures, including repositories with no third-party dependencies. Bound installation, cancellation and cleanup under the existing sandbox limits and execution allowances; a cold cache must not renew a deadline. Dependency preparation must not expose host credentials or unrelated host paths. Preserve Invariant's current module-cache behavior and per-build compilation-cache isolation.

Acceptance: cold installation, reuse without network installation, invalidation when any relevant input changes, concurrent cache creation, missing or inconsistent locks, install failure and cancellation. Record network use and image identity with a fake container runner; prove failed or incomplete preparations cannot be reused and that checks need no network after preparation.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Run each touched part's checks offline
issues.body:
Extend plumbing.Sandbox.Run to execute the configured repository checks using the contract and prepared dependency environments from the preceding issues. Run format, lint, build and the touched parts' test suites in their declared directories and digest-pinned toolchains, offline. Expose the same execution path to the builder's test tool and the factory's final check. Supply the trusted runner without assuming an arbitrary Go or Node image already contains Python or the host's Go cache.

Select parts from planned changes, acceptance files and admitted regression files through the shared ownership rules. A Go/TypeScript monorepo change confined to one part runs that part's suite; shared inputs select every affected part. Keep the existing Invariant Go package selection and scheduling path unchanged.

Preserve today's limits, cleanup and reporting: --init, 4 GiB memory, 1,024 processes, the twelve-minute whole-run deadline and shared ten-minute test-phase budget, with no reset per part or command. Preserve aggregate concurrency limits and shared build execution allowances. Report the part, phase and test identity where available, retaining partial results and unfinished work on timeout, interruption or failure. Command diagnostics must not impersonate result records. A failed format, lint, build or test command fails the check.

Acceptance: fake invocations show correct image, working directory, dependency environment, selected commands and network disabled for every check. Cover each failure phase, multiple parts sharing the budget, cancellation and container removal. Keep the existing Invariant sandbox budget, scheduling and evidence tests passing. Individual native acceptance-test evidence is added in the next issue.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Ratify and check acceptance tests in native frameworks
issues.body:
Generalize plumbing plans and their check to use tests in the configured repository's own framework. internal/plumbing/plan.go currently requires Go source, Test-prefixed names and Go AST declarations. Carry the part, framework and file-qualified test selector needed to run one acceptance test, supporting Go testing, pytest and TypeScript's Vitest/Jest conventions through the declared named-test command. Validate selectors without interpreting a test name as shell code.

Keep acceptance tests in new regular files, store their exact source and execution identity in the ratified plan, and prevent builders from editing them. Update draft reading, hashing, lock writing/reading, ratification consumers and sandbox reporting together. Existing Go plan hashes and ratified locks must remain valid without migration. Capture the relevant base configuration identity so a changed configuration cannot silently reinterpret a ratified test.

Extend the offline runner to execute each acceptance selector separately and obtain framework evidence that this test actually completed. Every test must fail on the base before proposal and pass on the candidate. Already-passing, absent, skipped, duplicate or ambiguous selections, zero-test success, incomplete runs, install/tool failures and timeouts are not base-failure evidence. Preserve the existing allowance for a completed compile failure caused by a proposed Go API; distinguish analogous attributable code failures from broken test setup.

Acceptance: Go, pytest, Vitest and Jest fixtures demonstrate independent fail-on-base/pass-after-change evidence. Same-named tests in different files or parts cannot satisfy one another. Forged diagnostic output cannot establish success. Source or selector tampering invalidates ratification, while existing Invariant locks and acceptance checks retain their behavior.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Apply repository test conventions to staging and scope
issues.body:
Extend the existing regression-test allowance to configured repositories, using the repository context and native tests from the preceding issues. A build may write its plan's named files and add new regular regression tests in the touched code's test scope, following that part's framework conventions. This must support Python test directories and TypeScript colocated or separate tests without treating arbitrary files in a part as writable tests.

Use one policy across internal/plumbing/stage.go, writable-file discovery, formatting, sandbox selection, final copying and internal/scope/scope.go. Determine additions against the original checkout throughout builder repairs, and against the diff's merge base in CI. A later repair may change or remove a regression test that this build added. Existing unnamed tests, other production files, unrelated parts, test configuration, ratified acceptance sources and plan records remain protected. Keep regular-file checks, including refusal of symbolic and hard links. Preserve Invariant's precise Go package and embedded-asset ownership behavior.

Acceptance: new conventional regression files are admitted and executed for Go, Python and TypeScript; a separate test directory can belong to touched source; unrelated tests and production files disguised as tests are refused. Exercise staging, copy-back and CI scope with the same cases. Cover repair removal, a base branch that deleted an existing test after divergence, a deleted package, changes outside the plan and attempts to change the pinned acceptance tests. The configured allowance must not depend on candidate edits to repository policy.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Hold each repository's trusted changes for a person
issues.body:
Use the base-branch repository contract to compute the trusted base for configured external repositories. Always include CI configuration and the gate workflow, .invariant/repository.json, repository agent rules such as root and nested AGENTS.md, and the file's additional trusted paths. Protect configuration that supplies agents' instructions or tools as well. Invariant continues to use its current plumbing.TrustedBase and current CI-path restrictions.

For configured external plumbing, allow explicitly planned CI files through plan validation and scope, while classifying them as human-merge changes. This replaces the unconditional .github rejection only for that profile. Document that publishing workflow changes requires credentials permitted to do so; ordinary plumbing does not require that permission. A missing permission must produce an actionable human handoff, never a ready or merged success. Keep Invariant's App permission policy unchanged.

Carry trusted classification through proposals, scope results, publication, retries and the last pre-merge check. Reuse the existing protocol's human-merge hold rather than changing its proved transitions. Recompute from actual changed paths and authoritative base rules, not the plan's displayed Trusted list. Candidate deletion or weakening of a trust declaration cannot authorize its own merge; revalidate against the current base before merging and stop on an incompatible configuration change.

Acceptance: repository-file, CI, root/nested agent-rule and custom-trusted edits wait for a person and their drafts are not automatically readied, including after retry. An ordinary in-scope change remains eligible for automatic merge. Cover removal of a trust entry, forged Trusted metadata and base movement. Invariant's existing trusted-path and CI-refusal tests retain their results. Update docs/factory-app.md for the external workflow-edit prerequisite.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Give planning, build and review agents repository context
issues.body:
Make plumbing agents and factory posts describe the repository they are working on. Use the trusted context from the base configuration for planning, initial builds, fallbacks, repairs and read-only reviews: applicable agent rules, which documents describe the current repository, part ownership, commands, native acceptance selectors, regression conventions and human-merge paths. Ensure repository rules actually reach each role's workspace and prompt without replacing the factory's immutable plan and scope boundaries.

Update internal/formalize/plan.go, internal/plumbing/prompt.go and their callers. Also adapt internal/factory/plancomments.go: proposals must show native test sources and selectors honestly, and pull requests must describe the configured checks rather than always promising gofmt/go vet. Include repository context in plans of issues where needed, while leaving modeled-project synthesis behavior alone.

Invariant's SPEC.md, README's 400-line budget, decision journal and merger-work rules apply to Invariant as today. Another repository follows its own declared rules and current-state documents; a file merely named SPEC.md or README.md does not import Invariant's policies. Do not add decision-followup automation: #452 leaves each step's decision to its merger.

Acceptance: inspect planner, builder, repair and reviewer requests for Go/Python/TypeScript repositories, including one without SPEC.md or decisions/ and a monorepo with nested rules. Their prompts and posts name the correct framework, checks and documents, and do not impose absent Invariant documents or Go-only test rules. Preserve the existing Invariant documentation/prompt tests and review/repair budgets.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Draft repository configuration with invariant init
issues.body:
Extend invariant init and internal/setup to draft .invariant/repository.json from the checkout for a person to review and commit. Build on the repository contract already implemented. Discover Go modules and go.sum, Python pyproject.toml or requirements.txt and available locks, and TypeScript package.json, scripts and lockfiles, including multiple parts in a monorepo. Avoid vendored dependencies, generated trees and installed environments during discovery.

Draft directories, languages, locked-install inputs and commands, native test conventions and current-state/rules references from evidence in the repository. Use maintained digest-pinned defaults where known, and clearly identify unresolved toolchain, lock or command fields for manual completion. An unresolved draft must not validate as an enabled configuration. Never present floating requirements as a lock or invent a working check when discovery is inconclusive. Discovery executes no repository scripts and installs nothing.

Retain init's non-overwrite behavior for existing customized files; rerunning on the same output is safe. Explain that a person reviews and commits the file on the base branch and that the gate must support these checks before plumbing is enabled. Keep existing modeled-project setup working. The next issue upgrades the generated gate; this issue supplies configuration discovery and drafting only.

Acceptance: fixtures cover Go, Python, TypeScript, a mixed monorepo, multiple supported lock conventions, missing locks or unknown commands, no detectable project and an existing edited configuration. Check digest pinning or explicit unresolved output, valid paths and ownership, no repository execution, and repeat/non-overwrite behavior.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Generate a CI gate for repository checks and plans
issues.body:
Complete the gate invariant init writes, using the configured sandbox checks and native plans from earlier steps. Add a CLI entry point suitable for CI that resolves the authoritative base configuration, selects affected parts for a factory PR, prepares locked dependencies and runs the declared checks and pinned acceptance tests with the same offline execution and failure reporting as factory builds. Ordinary CI runs must also check the repository, with full checks when no change selection is available.

Update internal/setup/gate.yml so invariant/gate fails when repository checks fail, runs scope for factory branches, and verifies ratification for plumbing plan records as well as modeled projects. Include repositories containing only plans and guard empty lists. Keep the pinned Invariant revision, read-only workflow permissions, modeled verification, receipt upload and existing job name. Candidate repository-file edits cannot weaken their own checks or skip scope or ratification.

Make the generated workflow usable with the init draft once a person completes it. Extend setup guidance and capability validation so an old gate that merely has the invariant/gate job name is not presented as sufficient for configured plumbing; report the required upgrade without rejecting existing modeled-only setup. Do not alter Invariant's own gate behavior.

Acceptance: generated-workflow and CLI fixtures for all three languages and the mixed monorepo exercise the real check selection and fake external processes. Missing or wrong plan ratification, changed pinned tests, out-of-plan edits and each configured check failure fail CI. A plan-only repository is ratified; an empty modeled-only repository does not invoke ratification with no arguments. Confirm native tests execute offline after dependency preparation, and the untouched monorepo part's suite is not run for a confined factory change.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Enable configured plumbing and exercise the complete factory flow
issues.body:
With configuration, sandbox, native plans, scope, trust, prompts and generated CI in place, replace the gitdek/invariant-only eligibility check in internal/factory/plumbing.go and factory.go. A GitHub repository with a valid committed base configuration and the required gate can take plumbing; do not force its language to Go. Pass one authoritative repository context through planning, ratification, building, review and publication, and revalidate at merge. Configuration found only on the issue branch or builder workspace cannot enable plumbing.

Retain today's unsupported answer and human-review label when an external repository has no file, with no agent run, proposal or build branch, including revisions. Malformed configuration or an obsolete gate gets a specific setup failure. Invariant's existing plumbing works without a repository file. Modeled-project builds, supported hosts and languages, and the existing protocol remain unchanged.

Add end-to-end fixtures for Go, Python and TypeScript that take a plumbing issue through the real planning check, hash ratification, build, review, scope and ready-PR publication against fake agents, GitHub and container processes. Follow the real Builder fixture in internal/factory/review_repair_accept_test.go rather than a builder that merely returns success. Each fixture's acceptance test must fail on the base and pass after the build. Assert lockfile installation and cache reuse, network only during installation, and offline checks. A Go/TypeScript fixture runs only the touched part's suite. Exercise out-of-plan refusal and human holds for repository-file, CI and agent-rule changes, including retry and a credential refusal for workflow publication.

Run the relevant existing Invariant plumbing, scope, ratification, setup and factory compatibility tests. Finish SPEC.md, the README and docs/factory.md with setup examples, the repository contract, native tests, trust and the no-file behavior, replacing D-0121's temporary limitation only now that it is removed. Hosted operation, other languages/hosts and decision-followup automation remain outside #452.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.
